about: Nine one-page homepages for two fictional products, for benchmarking the homepage craft critic (design_craft_bench). Which pages carry which measurable craft problems is kept off the box.

brief.disclosure: Fictional pottery studio made for a design study: no real classes, bookings or payments.
brief.audience: Adults who have never touched clay, or tried it once and want to start again, choosing a first class.
brief.purpose: Show the three ways to start, what a class is like and what it costs, so a beginner books a taster class with confidence.

concept.name: Studio noticeboard
concept.brief: Warm, handmade and calm: an editorial serif over cream and sand, clay-red actions, ink bands for emphasis, generous space and simple flat illustrations of pots. It should feel like a small studio's well-kept noticeboard, not a marketplace.
concept.signature_move: A large serif headline beside a flat illustration of pots on a shelf; the clay colour marks every action.
concept.motion: Class cards rise gently into place on load (reduced motion respected).
concept.imagery: Flat inline SVG illustration of pots; no photos.

brief.disclosure: Fictional product made for a design study: no real accounts, alerts or payments.
brief.audience: Engineering leads at small software companies who want customers to hear about outages from them first.
brief.purpose: Show how a status page works with the tools the team already uses and what it costs, so a lead starts a free page.

concept.name: Night console
concept.brief: Confident and technical without being cold: chunky grotesque headlines on deep navy, one electric lime action colour, panels that read like a calm console, and a live-looking status board as proof.
concept.signature_move: A live-looking status board in the hero; lime marks every action.
concept.motion: Feature cards rise gently into place on load (reduced motion respected).
concept.imagery: Interface fragments built in HTML/CSS and simple line icons; no photos.
